scenes.visual: THE WORLD, kept for both films (16:9, dark navy background). Pale morph (typica) = warm CREAM moth; dark morph (carbonaria) = CHARCOAL moth with a thin white outline; birds = one simple BLUE bird silhouette; wasps (second film) = ORANGE. Every fitness axis is labelled 'relative fitness'. The word 'morph' is used on screen, never 'form' or 'type'. Cartoons and labelled blocks only; anything not computed carries a small 'schematic' tag. Title card 'Selection Has an Agent' fades in over a single grey-brown tree trunk.

scenes.tts: Birds eat more dark moths than pale ones on these trees. Is that evolution? Not yet. This film builds the answer one piece at a time.
scenes.visual: A tree trunk covered in pale green-grey lichen. Several CREAM and CHARCOAL moths rest on it. The BLUE bird swoops in and takes a CHARCOAL moth. On-screen question: 'Is that evolution?'
scenes.narration: Birds eat more dark moths than pale ones on these trees. Is that evolution? Not yet. This film builds the answer one piece at a time.

scenes.tts: Meet the peppered moth. It comes in two main colour morphs. A morph is one distinct form within a species. The pale morph is called typica. The dark morph is called carbonaria. Intermediate moths exist too, but we follow these two. Both rest by day on tree trunks.
scenes.caption: Meet the peppered moth. It comes in two main colour morphs. A morph is one distinct form within a species. The pale morph is called typica. The dark morph is called carbonaria. Intermediate moths exist too, but we follow these two. Both rest by day on tree trunks.
scenes.visual: Zoom to two moths side by side, labelled 'typica (pale morph)' in CREAM and 'carbonaria (dark morph)' in CHARCOAL. Small tag beneath: 'two main morphs; intermediates exist'. A small parent-to-offspring arrow under each shows the colour passing down. Two labels pin to the corner of the frame: 'variation' and 'inheritance'.
scenes.narration: Meet the peppered moth. It comes in two main colour morphs. A morph is one distinct form within a species. The pale morph is called typica. The dark morph is called carbonaria. Intermediate moths exist too, but we follow these two. Both rest by day on tree trunks.

scenes.tts: Birds hunt these moths by sight. On a trunk covered in pale lichen, the dark morph stands out. So birds find more dark moths than pale ones. The bird is the agent. The lichen-covered trunk is the environment.
scenes.visual: Back to the lichen trunk. CHARCOAL moths pulse slightly to show they stand out; CREAM moths blend in. The BLUE bird picks off CHARCOAL moths one by one. Labels pin to the frame: 'agent: birds' and 'environment: lichen bark'.
scenes.narration: Birds hunt these moths by sight. On a trunk covered in pale lichen, the dark morph stands out. So birds find more dark moths than pale ones. The bird is the agent. The lichen-covered trunk is the environment.

scenes.tts: Fitness is reproductive success compared with other variants. Here we measure one part of it, survival through a day. A dial shows the ratio: dark survival divided by pale survival. On lichen, the dial sits below one. Fitness is relative. What matters is how one morph does compared with another in the same place.
scenes.visual: Beside the trunk, a two-bar 'survivors' meter (CREAM bar taller than CHARCOAL bar) and a semicircular dial labelled 'dark survival / pale survival', with a mark at 1. The needle settles below 1. No number is shown on the needle. A fourth label pins to the frame: 'fitness difference'.
scenes.narration: Fitness is reproductive success compared with other variants. Here we measure one part of it, survival through a day. A dial shows the ratio: dark survival divided by pale survival. On lichen, the dial sits below one. Fitness is relative. What matters is how one morph does compared with another in the same place.

scenes.tts: Now change the environment, not the moths. In the nineteenth century, air pollution killed the lichens around British industrial cities. Soot coated the bark. On dark bark, the pale morph stands out instead. The dial swings above one, and the dark morph became common there.
scenes.caption: Now change the environment, not the moths. In the 19th century, air pollution killed the lichens around British industrial cities. Soot coated the bark. On dark bark, the pale morph stands out instead. The dial swings above one, and the dark morph became common there.
scenes.visual: Smoke drifts across; the lichen fades and the trunk turns sooty black. Now CREAM moths stand out and the BLUE bird takes them. The dial needle swings above 1; the CHARCOAL survivors bar grows taller. Tag: '19th century, industrial Britain'.
scenes.narration: Now change the environment, not the moths. In the 19th century, air pollution killed the lichens around British industrial cities. Soot coated the bark. On dark bark, the pale morph stands out instead. The dial swings above one, and the dark morph became common there.

scenes.tts: Then, in the late twentieth century, air pollution fell and the lichens grew back. Which morph do the birds now take more often?
scenes.caption: Then, in the late 20th century, air pollution fell and the lichens grew back. Which morph do the birds now take more often?
scenes.visual: The smoke clears; lichen creeps back over the trunk. The bird hovers, waiting. The dial needle trembles at 1. On-screen: 'Which morph now?'
scenes.narration: Then, in the late 20th century, air pollution fell and the lichens grew back. Which morph do the birds now take more often?

scenes.visual: Hold on the lichen trunk with both morphs resting and the bird hovering. A small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: The dark morph again. It stands out on lichen, so the dial swings back below one, and carbonaria declined. Same moth, same birds. A different environment favoured a different colour. Fitness belongs to the moth in a place.
scenes.visual: The bird takes CHARCOAL moths again; the dial needle swings back below 1; the CHARCOAL bar shrinks. Text: 'Same moth, same birds, different environment'. The fourth label updates to 'agent in an environment'.
scenes.narration: The dark morph again. It stands out on lichen, so the dial swings back below one, and carbonaria declined. Same moth, same birds. A different environment favoured a different colour. Fitness belongs to the moth in a place.

scenes.tts: Notice what the birds did not do. They did not make any dark or pale moths. Like a sieve, they sorted moths that already existed. That sorting, within one generation, is selection. A drought does not create deep beaks either. It removes more of the shallow ones.
scenes.visual: A sieve drops over the trunk's moths; CREAM and CHARCOAL moths pour in, some fall through and vanish, survivors stay in the mesh. Label: 'selection = sorting within one generation'. Nothing new appears in the sieve.
scenes.narration: Notice what the birds did not do. They did not make any dark or pale moths. Like a sieve, they sorted moths that already existed. That sorting, within one generation, is selection. A drought does not create deep beaks either. It removes more of the shallow ones.

scenes.tts: Is it evolution yet? Only if offspring resemble their parents. Picture two futures. In one, colour is inherited, and the young of the survivors can carry some of the shift. In the other, colour is not inherited, so the shift need not pass to the young.
scenes.visual: Below the sieve, the survivors split into two rows of offspring. Top row, tagged 'colour inherited': arrows carry colour from the survivors to their offspring, but the offspring's colour mix is drawn as a '?' labelled 'response depends on genotypes, mating and inheritance'; the row shows only that an inherited response is possible, not that offspring copy the survivors' mix. Bottom row, tagged 'schematic: if colour were not inherited': offspring drawn as grey outlines with a '?' over them, no colour mix implied. A grey 'no inherited response' stamp lands on the bottom row.
scenes.narration: Is it evolution yet? Only if offspring resemble their parents. Picture two futures. In one, colour is inherited, and the young of the survivors can carry some of the shift. In the other, colour is not inherited, so the shift need not pass to the young.

scenes.tts: So a full selection argument has four parts. Variation, inheritance, a fitness difference, and an agent in an environment. An agent sorts variants by fitness. Inheritance carries the sorting forward.
scenes.visual: The four labels collected through the film fly into a stack: 'variation', 'inheritance', 'fitness difference', 'agent in an environment'. An arrow from 'an agent sorts variants by fitness' to 'inheritance carries the sorting forward'.
scenes.narration: So a full selection argument has four parts. Variation, inheritance, a fitness difference, and an agent in an environment. An agent sorts variants by fitness. Inheritance carries the sorting forward.

scenes.visual: End card over the dimmed lichen trunk, large white text, centred: 'An agent sorts variants by fitness; inheritance carries the sorting forward.'
